generic_sampling_rules.integer_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1; unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_foreign_key: Sample from the parent table's generated primary-key values; include at least one NULL row when the column is nullable; otherwise every value must exist in the parent.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Positive integers in [1, 100]; include boundary values around any listed literal (literal-1, literal, literal+1).
generic_sampling_rules.real_amount: Non-negative real values in [0.0, 5000.0] with one decimal place; include 0.0 and values near listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.real_year: Real-valued years in [1900.0, 2025.0] with one decimal place; ascending order where a date-order rule applies.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Short human-readable names drawn from a small pool of 8-12 distinct strings; allow near-duplicate variants (case, spacing, suffix) and a NULL share when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Values drawn only from the explicit enum list for that column.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one generated row has NULL; overall NULL share follows the compact database's observed share (0.0 in the sample, so keep NULLs sparse but present).

per_column_exceptions.targets: Include at least two rows tied at the maximum Market_Rate value (rank 1 in DESC order) and at least two rows tied at rank 2; values must be distinct enough that MAX is well-defined.
At least two rows share the maximum Market_Rate value so a MAX-derived join returns >= 2 qualifying rows; also include rows with different values.
Include at least one furniture row whose Market_Rate does not match any derived max_rate value (parent row without child in the derived join).
Include at least one manufacturer row with no matching furniture_manufacte row (parent without children); child rows must reference existing manufacturers (no NULL FK).
Include rows where Manufacturer_ID equals itself (trivially true) and rows one step from a listed boundary value.
Include at least one manufacturer with no furniture_manufacte children; also include manufacturers with 1, 2, and >=3 children to satisfy group_sizes.
Ensure group sizes of 1, 2, and >=3 when grouping furniture_manufacte by Manufacturer_ID.
Include at least two manufacturers whose MAX(Price_in_Dollar) over their children is tied at rank 1 in DESC order.
Include at least two furniture rows tied at rank 2 in DESC order of Furniture_ID.
Include at least one furniture row with no furniture_manufacte child.
20-50% of furniture.Name values are duplicates of another row's Name (so DISTINCT reduces the count).
Include at least one furniture row with no furniture_manufacte child; child Furniture_ID values must exist in furniture.
At least two rows share the maximum Price_in_Dollar value so a MAX-derived scalar comparison returns >= 2 qualifying rows.
Include at least two rows tied at rank 1 in DESC order of Price_in_Dollar.
20-50% of manufacturer.Name values are duplicates of another row's Name.
Include at least two rows tied at rank 100 in ASC order of Name (requires >= 100 rows or a tie at the LIMIT boundary; if fewer rows, ensure the last row is tied with another).
Include at least two rows tied at rank 100 in ASC order of Open_Year (or at the LIMIT boundary if fewer rows).
Include values 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11 to cover predicates < 6 and > 10 and their boundaries.
At least two rows with different Num_of_Factories values so SUM and AVG are well-defined over >= 2 rows.
Ensure group sizes of 1, 2, and >=3 when grouping by Num_of_Shops.
Include at least two manufacturers whose MAX(Price_in_Dollar) over children is tied at rank 1 in DESC order, grouped by Num_of_Shops.

generation_specification.uncertainty: The sample has no NULLs, but nullable columns may take NULL; NULL share is kept sparse. No calculated-column formula is supported by the shown rows, so none is stated. The tie-at-rank-100 targets for manufacturer.Name and Open_Year require at least 100 rows or a tie at the LIMIT boundary; with only 7 rows per instance, the tie is placed at the last rank.

issues.evidence: Specification per_column_exceptions for furniture.Market_Rate ties_for_order_limit requires 'at least two rows tied at rank 2' in DESC order. spec.py _build_furniture sets rates[2]=rates[3]=40.0 only when n>=4, which holds (n=7), so rank-2 tie is constructed. However the spec also says 'values must be distinct enough that MAX is well-defined' — satisfied since 52.5 > 40.0. No blocking issue; noted for completeness.
issues.requested_revision: None required; the construction satisfies the stated tie targets.

issues.evidence: Specification ties_for_order_limit for manufacturer.Name and manufacturer.Open_Year target rank 100 with LIMIT(100), but table_sizes_per_instance sets manufacturer=7. The spec's own uncertainty note acknowledges this and places the tie at the last rank. This is a documented, self-consistent relaxation, not an error.
issues.requested_revision: None required; the spec explicitly documents the boundary-tie fallback for small tables.

issues.evidence: cli.py contains dead/broken code: _one() references undefined names G_ORIG, G_SCHEMA, inst_placeholder, G_SEED and is never called (main uses _worker/_generate_one). This is unreachable dead code and does not affect execution (returncode 0, 20/20 valid).
issues.requested_revision: Remove the unused _one() function to avoid confusion; not blocking.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows furniture_manufacte rows_skipped=2 across 20 instances (98 added vs 100 expected). This is the PK-dedup path in _build_furniture_manufacte / sample_fresh_primary_keys dropping a duplicate (Manufacturer_ID, Furniture_ID) pair. Integrity checks report 0 duplicate keys and 0 FK violations, so the skip is benign, but it slightly reduces the intended 5 rows/instance for that table.
issues.requested_revision: Optionally make the child-row planner guarantee distinct (Manufacturer_ID, Furniture_ID) pairs so all 5 rows are inserted; not blocking since integrity is preserved.

issues.evidence: NULL rule: feedback shows every nullable column has NULL 20/140 (or 20/98) generated rows, i.e. exactly one NULL per instance per column, matching the sparse-NULL intent. NOT NULL/PK columns have no NULLs (0 not_null violations). Compliant with the interface NULL rule.

unresolved_checks: construction_pairs: 10 of 34 eligible pairs separated; the remaining 24 are not separated in the sampled instances. Per instructions, missing separation alone does not establish a generation error, and no held-out labels were used, so this is left as an open observation rather than a blocking issue.
The rank-100 tie targets for manufacturer.Name/Open_Year cannot be literally satisfied with 7 rows; the spec's documented last-rank fallback is accepted but the literal rank-100 behavior is untested.
